items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1961-08-15
items.q: Me and Mealy Bones was playing with him... I played with Thomas.

ctx.x: Was that during the last war or about when was the memory of that?

Yeah, well that was during the last war. Me and Mealy Bones was playing with him. Mealy was playing clarinet and I was playing sax. And Thomas had nice work. In fact he had more work than he could really do. Because we was going down by every Saturday around wrestling, playing for old man LeBlanc. That was a nickel dance too. The nickel dance was popular, you know what I mean, at that time. Especially all throughout the country. We only had a couple of them here in the city. But everywhere you went out of town to…
Where was that on Grand Isle? The theater?
I was going to ask some more. You were talking about these bands like working with Kid Thomas. You might as well go on from there. Is there anything else you want to continue along that line?

Well, yeah, like I said, I played with Thomas. I made more money with him than any band I played with. How kind of money did you make? Did Kips, you mean? Well, in average it was more money but less money. You see, the skills wasn't like it is now. We wasn't in the union. And we was making around $8 and $10 going out of town. That's why we was getting more out of town work, you see. And we played the jobs around there in town. Some of them wasn't paying but a dollar and a dollar and a quarter a night. Two…
Was that in the Depression or during the war or before the war? Well, that was... When you were paying a dollar and a dollar and a half an hour, it must have been Depression, but it did.
